ferramentas.resumo: Read the current drawing's name, path, extents and object counts.
Start a drawing: blank with the engineering layers, or from a bundled/own template.
Load an existing DXF from disk (DWG only on the live AutoCAD backend).
Write the drawing back to its file, or to a path you give.
Save a copy under a new name; the extension picks DXF, DWG or DWT.
Write a DXF interchange copy of the drawing.
Plot the drawing, or one paper-space layout, to PDF.
Strip unused layers, blocks, linetypes and styles out of the file.
Scan the drawing for structural errors and repair what it finds.
Close the drawing, saving first unless you say otherwise.
Step back one operation.
Reapply the operation you just undid.
Draw a straight line between two points.
Draw a circle: a hole, a bore, a pitch circle.
Draw a circular arc from a centre, a radius and two angles.
Draw a connected outline or closed profile through a list of points.
Draw a closed rectangle from two opposite corners.
Place a single-line text label.
Place a wrapped paragraph note in a text box of a given width.
Place a parts list, BOM or schedule as a table with headers and rows.
Add a callout: an arrow with a note on the end.
Fill a closed boundary with a section pattern such as ANSI31 or SOLID.
Draw a smooth NURBS curve through fit points.
Draw an ellipse from its centre, major axis vector and axis ratio.
Place a point marker (node) at a coordinate.
Drop an instance of an existing block definition into the drawing.
Replace a hatch's fill with a two-colour gradient.
Change a hatch's pattern, scale, angle, colour or island style.
Add a boundary path to a hatch, arcs and ellipses included.
Mask whatever is behind a closed polygon on the sheet.
Draw a revision cloud around an area.
Dimension a horizontal or vertical size, with an ISO 129 tolerance or ISO 286 fit.
Dimension the true distance between two points, along a slope.
Dimension the included angle between two rays from a vertex.
Call out the radius of a circle or arc, optionally toleranced.
Call out a hole or shaft diameter, optionally to a fit such as H7.
Shift an entity by a displacement vector.
Duplicate an entity and offset the copy.
Turn an entity about a base point by an angle in degrees.
Resize an entity uniformly about a base point.
Reflect an entity across a mirror line, keeping or dropping the original.
Make a parallel copy of a line, circle or polyline at a set distance.
Cut a line back to where another crosses it, keeping the side you point at.
Lengthen a line until it meets a boundary line.
Round a corner between two lines with a tangent arc.
Bevel a corner between two lines by two setback distances.
Erase one entity by handle.
Repeat an entity in a grid of rows and columns.
Repeat an entity around a centre: a bolt circle or radial pattern.
Change an entity's layer, colour, linetype, lineweight or visibility.
Reword a label, or change its height or rotation, keeping its handle.
Put an opaque background box behind an MTEXT.
Find and replace text across the drawing.
Change a circle's radius, a line's endpoints or an arc's angles in place.
Select entities inside or crossing a rectangle.
Select entities inside or crossing an arbitrary polygon.
Select entities by layer, type, colour, linetype or minimum area.
Inspect one entity by handle: type, layer, colour and geometry.
Browse the drawing's entities and their handles, filtered by type or layer.
Erase a whole list of entities in one call.
Read what the user already picked in the AutoCAD viewport (COM backend).
Read an entity's extended data (XDATA) by application name.
Attach or replace extended data (XDATA) on an entity.
List every layer with its colour, linetype and visibility state.
Add a layer with a colour, linetype and lineweight.
Remove an empty layer from the drawing.
Choose the layer that new geometry lands on.
Change an existing layer's colour, linetype or lineweight.
Freeze a layer so it stops drawing and regenerating.
Bring a frozen layer back into view.
Lock a layer so its entities can be seen but not edited.
Unlock a layer so its entities can be edited again.
Turn a layer off so its entities stop showing.
Turn a layer that was switched off back on.
Hide every layer except one, to work on it alone.
List the dash patterns currently loaded in the drawing.
Load a linetype such as CENTER or HIDDEN, without the FILEDIA dialog trap.
List the block definitions the drawing already carries.
Place a block, filling in its attribute values as you go.
Break a block reference apart into its component entities.
Read the tag/value pairs off a block reference.
Fill in a block reference's attributes, such as title-block fields.
Turn existing entities into a reusable block definition.
Define a block from typed primitives and attribute definitions, on both engines.
Find every place a given block is inserted.
Trace the closed boundary around a point, like BOUNDARY.
Join named entities into one closed boundary polyline.
Dump every DXF property of one entity, like LIST.
Count the drawing's objects, broken down by type and by layer.
List everything that falls inside a rectangular window.
Measure the gap between two points: distance, dx/dy and angle.
Measure a polygon's area and perimeter from its vertices.
Area and perimeter of an existing entity, by handle.
Get the overall extents of everything drawn.
Grab the handles of everything sitting on one layer.
Grab the handles of every entity of one type: all the circles, all the lines.
Report how many entities, and which types, sit on each layer.
Run an ordered list of tool calls in one round trip, binding results between steps.
Draw many entities in one call instead of one round trip each.
Move, rotate, scale, restyle or delete many entities in one call.
Create a standard layer set: architectural, mechanical, electrical or piping.
Show the available layer templates and the layers in each.
Sanity-check the drawing for empty layers, zero-length lines and duplicates.
Zoom out until every entity fits on screen.
Zoom in on a rectangular region of the drawing.
Capture a PNG picture of the drawing as it currently looks.
Fit the drawing on screen, then capture it: the quickest visual check.
Open a rollback checkpoint before a risky edit.
Keep the changes and drop the checkpoint.
Throw away every change made since transaction_begin.
Check the connection: which engine is live and what document is open.
Ask the active backend which features it really supports.
Read one AutoCAD system variable, such as DIMSCALE or LTSCALE.
Set one AutoCAD system variable by name.
Read or change drawing units, precision, linetype and dimension scale by name.
Send a raw command string to the AutoCAD command line (COM only).
Evaluate an AutoLISP expression inside AutoCAD (COM only).
See what this server can do: version, tool groups and active profile.
Draw a helical gear front view: true involute teeth, circles, bore and keyway.
Draw a straight-tooth spur gear front view with true involute teeth.
Draw the hatched side cross-section A-A of a gear you already drew.
Draw a bore with a DIN 6885 keyway, auto-sized from the bore diameter.
Draw the side cross-section of a keyed bore.
Stamp an ISO 7200 title block and sheet frame onto an A3 drawing.
Finish the drawing: validate, critique, save, screenshot and score it.
Hand the drawing off: a hashed, validated bundle of files plus a manifest.
Check the brief before you draw: units, part type, tolerances, missing inputs.
Commit sheet size, scale, layer set and dimension style before any geometry.
Review the drawing for drafting mistakes: must come back empty before finalize.
Auto-repair what the critique found, then re-check, up to three rounds.
Get an exact endpoint, midpoint, centre, quadrant or perpendicular foot.
Find where two lines or circles cross, exactly.
Find where a line from an outside point touches a circle.
Lay down an infinite guide line to build geometry against.
Wipe the construction scaffolding off the drawing before finalize.
Set up a standard ISO layer set with the right colours and lineweights.
Dimension a set of entities at once, as a chain, baseline or ordinate run.
Pick every entity matching a description: type, layer, colour, length, location.
Draw an ISO 1101 feature control frame: symbol, tolerance zone and datums.
Mark a datum on a feature: filled triangle plus the boxed datum letter.
List the sheet tabs: Model plus every paper-space layout.
Add a new paper-space sheet tab to the drawing.
Switch to a sheet tab, or back to model space.
Put a scaled window onto model space on a sheet, at 1:1, 1:2 and so on.
Delete a sheet tab and everything drawn on it.
Rename a sheet tab, keeping its geometry and handles.
Duplicate a sheet with its page setup and geometry.
List the viewports on a sheet with their scales and locks.
Set a viewport's scale, e.g. 1:2 or 1:50.
Lock a viewport so its scale cannot be zoomed away.
Remove a viewport from a sheet.
Move entities between model space and a sheet through a viewport.
Create a 3D solid box (live AutoCAD, opt-in via ENABLE_3D).
Create a 3D solid cylinder or shaft (live AutoCAD, opt-in via ENABLE_3D).
Pull a closed profile up into a 3D solid (live AutoCAD, opt-in via ENABLE_3D).
Spin a closed profile around an axis into a 3D solid (opt-in via ENABLE_3D).
Union, subtract or intersect two 3D solids; the tool solid is consumed.
List the P&ID symbol catalogue: families, variants, ports, parameters.
Place a P&ID symbol (valve, pump, vessel, instrument bubble, connector) as a tagged block with ports.
Draw a P&ID line port-to-port: orthogonal route, ISA-5.1 class, line number, markers, arrow.
Read the P&ID back as a graph: symbols, lines, junctions, dangling ends, confidence.
Instrument index derived from the P&ID graph (tag, function, loop, connections); optional CSV.
Line list derived from the P&ID graph (number, class, size, spec, from/to); optional CSV.
Equipment list derived from the P&ID graph (tag, kind, ports, connections); optional CSV.
Draw a whole P&ID from one declarative spec in one transaction; returns graph + critique.
Parse an ISA-5.1 instrument tag or an equipment tag; explains every letter.
List dimension styles with their ISO-25/ANSI variables and the current one.
Create a dimension style from the ISO-25 or ANSI preset, with per-variable overrides.
Change DIM* variables on an existing dimension style; reports only what moved.
Make a dimension style current so new dimensions use it.
List text styles: font file, height, width factor, oblique angle.
Create a text style from a bundled font (isocp, isocpeur, arial, romans) or any file.
Make a text style current so new text uses it.
List multileader styles: arrow size, landing gap, text style and height.
Create a multileader style from the ISO or ANSI preset, on both engines.
Put the drawing on ISO or ANSI in one call: dimstyle, text style, units, mech layers.
Read each sheet's page setup: paper, orientation, ctb, scale, device.
Set a sheet's paper, orientation, ctb, plot scale and device (PAGESETUP).
List the plot style tables (ctb): the AutoCAD catalogue, plus what is installed.
Plot every sheet (or the named ones) to PDF; each sheet size is read back from its PDF.
List the five bundled drawing templates: standard, sheet, layers, styles, page setup.
Save the current drawing as a template: .dwt on live AutoCAD, .dxf headlessly.
List the open documents: which is active, which have unsaved changes.
Switch which open document every later tool call targets.
Close one open document by name; never drops unsaved work unless told to.
Save the layer table (on/frozen/locked/colour/linetype/lineweight/plot + current) under a name, in the file.
Restore a saved layer state, all properties or a chosen subset.
List the layer states saved in this drawing.
Delete one saved layer state from the drawing.
Save a named view: a centre and height (and width) to come back to.
Restore a named view.
List the named views saved in this drawing.
List the user coordinate systems, with the implicit world one.
Define (or replace) a named UCS from an origin and two perpendicular axes, and make it current.
Make a saved UCS current, or `world` to reset to WCS.
Attach to the running AutoCAD or start it, optionally opening a file (live only).
Read AutoCAD preferences from the whitelist (OPTIONS dialog values; live only).
Change one whitelisted AutoCAD preference; reports old and new (live only).
Ask the operator to pick a point on screen (live only; blocks until they do).
Ask the operator to select one entity or a set on screen (live only).
Print a message on AutoCAD's command line (live only).
Explain a system variable: type, range, default, where it is saved, which engine honours it.
Read the drawing's title, subject, author, keywords, comments and custom properties.
Set the drawing's summary fields and add, change or delete custom properties.
Draw a machine part from a segment list or an outline plus typed features.
Add another view of a drawn part: side, top, section (full/half/offset) or detail.
Dimension a drawn part: ISO 129 dimensions, ISO 286 fits, a hole table.
Draw a linear, grid or polar hole pattern with centre marks on any drawing.
Draw a whole mechanical sheet - several parts and their views - in one transaction.
Read the part model back off the drawing: segments, features, views, omissions.
Search the standard-parts catalogue: ISO bolts, nuts, washers, cap screws, bearings.
Insert an ISO standard part - hex bolt, nut, washer, cap screw or ball bearing - as a tagged block.
Draw a standard feature - thread, undercut, ring or O-ring groove, centre hole - onto existing geometry.
Draw an ISO 21920-1 surface-texture symbol: Ra/Rz, process, lay, allowance.
Draw an ISO 2553 weld symbol: reference line, identification line, size and pitch.
Draw ISO 128-23 centre marks or centre lines on circles, read from the drawing.
Draw an ISO 128-40 cutting-plane line and return the plane the section view uses.
Hatch a region with the ISO 128-50 section pattern for a named material.
Draw an ISO 5457 sheet frame with the zone grid and centring marks.
Stamp an ISO 7200 title block (and frame) on any sheet from A4 to A0.
Append a revision row, with optional revision clouds and triangular tags.
Read the bill of materials out of the drawing's block references.
Draw the parts list as a real TABLE above the title block.
Add an ISO 6433 balloon linked to its item row.
Attach a DWG/DXF as an external reference (attachment or overlay).
List, reload, bind, detach or repath an external reference.
Attach a raster image (PNG/JPG) as an underlay.
Write the bill of materials to a CSV file, or to XLSX when openpyxl is present.
Write the drawing as a real DWG at a chosen AutoCAD version.
Add walls to the plan: clean L/T/X junctions, cut openings, material poché.
Host a door or a window in a drawn wall by distance along it; the wall is cut.
Draw a straight, L or U stair in plan and report its Blondel step rule.
Dimension the plan's facades: openings, walls and overall chains outside each side.
Label a room with its name, number and measured area.
Find the rooms of any plan and measure them; never modifies it.
Draw a door, window or room schedule from the plan records.
Search the furniture and sanitary catalogue in English or Turkish.
Insert a furniture or sanitary item - bed, sofa, WC, basin, bathtub - as a block.
Draw a structural grid: axis lines with numbered and lettered bubbles at both ends.
Draw a plan symbol: north arrow, section mark, level mark or elevation mark.
Draw a whole floor plan - walls, doors, windows, stairs, rooms, chains, schedules - in one transaction.
Read a foreign drawing: units, extents, clusters, layers, tags, rooms, languages.
Is this drawing to scale against a reference? Tag distances, ratios, a verdict.
Compare two revisions of a drawing: what moved, changed, was added or removed.
Find dangling ends, near misses and unjoined crossings in a pipe or cable network.
Pipe takeoff from a P&ID and its layout: rows by room, service and diameter.
Cable takeoff: one row per load, Manhattan length to its panel, rounded up to the metre.
